_note: The bought soldier (Sci-Fi Modular Soldier by AC Game Assets; Phase 21, docs/OVERNIGHT_BRIEF_SOLDIER_AND_VERTICAL_CENTRE.md section 3): SpeedKills' only player character when its files are here (npm run paid makes them, locally; they never enter git), the figures of before when they are not. src/game/soldier.ts loads it and builds its materials; src/game/retarget.ts carries the game's clips over to its rig. version is added to every paid file's address, since the game server keeps /models/ for a day and a re-import would otherwise be a day late.
_retry: Seconds waited before each try again at the soldier's files when one fails: a page loaded while a deploy swapped them found them missing once and settled on the old figures for the whole session (the owner, 2026-10-02: "we are the base model again? ... i just started a game and was the old model?"). Three more tries over 13 s outlast a deploy's swap; a page waits on the soldier before a match, so the tries are spent before anyone plays. A file missing on a local server is a checkout without the bought assets and is not tried again.
_rename: Its head bone is named head; the game's figures and clips name it Head, and code looks it up by that name (mannequin.ts, outfit.ts, gear.ts, the e2e), so it is renamed as it loads.
_measured: Off soldier.glb at rest by tools/checks/soldier.ts, which fails if the model and these differ: the height from the feet to the top of the head, the pelvis bone's height, the distance between the two upperarm bones, and the ball of the foot's height.
_parts: The model's 18 pieces (triangles), each a skinned mesh on the one skeleton, and the material slot each uses.
_scale: The hit boxes are fixed numbers built for a 1.829 m figure (dummy.ts, H); the soldier stands 1.845 m (measured above), so it is drawn at 1.829 / 1.845, and a headshot lands on its head without moving any hit box.
_tint: How the pack colours it, rebuilt (its Shader Graphs multiply the base colour by a tint wherever a mask is white): the armour by the armour colour (mask R) and the accent (the helmet mask, G); the suit by the suit colour; the head by the skin tone. Colours are sRGB hex; the pack's defaults are the first of each list, converted from its linear values.
_collar: The collar behind the head brought down (the owner, 2026-10-11: "ensure 100% of the head is visible from the back, i want to always be able to clearly snipe hs someone from the back"). Measured off the model in its bind pose (above the pelvis): the head's lowest point behind the neck at 0.696 m (0.672 round to the sides as far as the collar is lowered, the cut's mark), the body armour's collar rising behind it to 0.746 and the suit's to 0.714, so from 30 m behind a standing soldier's armour hid 36 of every 100 points of the back of its head, and from 30 degrees to the side up to 85. Each of `parts` above `below` metres under that lowest point keeps `keep` of its height over it, all the way round the back and the sides of the neck and fading out toward its front: fully where the way from the neck's line out to it is `front[0]` or less (a cosine) from straight ahead, not at all from `front[1]`, so the front of the collar and the chest stay as they are (soldier.ts collarLowering). Measured after, standing: 2 cm under the head left the armour 4 cm over its lowest point behind (the pose holds the head lower against the collar than the bind pose does), 7 cm under cleared it (`below` 8); lowered behind only, the collar's sides still hid 11 to 14 of every 100 points of the head from 30 degrees to a side.
_collarNeck: The collar is never lowered past the bottom edge of the neck's skin: `overNeck` metres over it, the edge's height the middle of its lowest points round the back and the sides within `neckRadius` m of the neck's line (soldier.ts collarLowering). Measured in the bind pose (over the neck bone): the edge 3 mm behind, -1 at the sides, -16 two thirds of the way round; the cut under the head alone (`below`) put the collar's top 51 to 55 mm under it all round the back and sides, a gap you could see the world through from behind, the owner's find in third person (2026-10-12). For the suit alone (`overNeckParts`): the armour over it keeps the cut under the head, since brought up with the suit its collar hid 0.5 to 3.6 of every 100 points of the skull from 30 m behind standing, walking, sprinting, crouched and aimed (VANGUARD), where 0.5 at most may be hidden; with the suit over the edge, the armour lower shows the suit's collar, not a gap. And the suit's cut at the edge itself (`overNeck` 0): 1.5 cm over it, its collar hid 0.7 of every 100 points of RUNNER's skull aimed, 0.8 cm over, 0.5, and at the edge none; there the squashed collar's top still stands 0 to 5 mm over the edge's middle round the back and the sides, and no ray goes through to the world in 240 shots of every gun (the skfigure e2e).
_variants: The four the player picks from (the owner: 4 variants, allowing us to change certain things), each a set of the model's pieces and default colours (indexes into the palettes). hide lists the pieces a variant leaves off. The toggles the player has on top of a variant are the helmet, the shoulder plates and the pouches.
